paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Mountain, Torah, and Peace Among the Nations

answers: In the top of the mountains
In the fields of Babylon
Under the hills
easy.explanation: The mountain of the LORD’s house will be established in the top of the mountains.
easy.q: Where will the mountain of the house of the LORD be established?

answers: Go up to the mountain of the LORD
Build a wall around Jerusalem
Return to their own lands
easy.explanation: They will say, “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD.”
easy.q: What will many nations ask to do?

answers: Plowshares
Crowns
Shields
easy.explanation: The nations will beat their swords into plowshares.
easy.q: What will swords be beaten into?

answers: His ways
The art of war
How to build cities
medium.explanation: The LORD will teach them of His ways.
medium.q: What will the LORD teach the nations?

answers: They will learn war no more
They will leave Jerusalem forever
They will build stronger weapons
medium.explanation: The nations will not lift up swords against one another or learn war anymore.
medium.q: What will happen after the nations are judged and rebuked?

answers: Every man will sit under his vine and fig tree
Every man will hide in a fortress
Every man will move to Babylon
medium.explanation: Everyone will sit under his vine and fig tree, and none will make them afraid.
medium.q: How is the future security of the people described?

answers: To learn His ways and walk in His paths
To conquer Jerusalem
To escape from famine
challenge.explanation: They will seek the LORD’s instruction so they may walk in His paths.
challenge.q: Why will the nations go to the mountain of the LORD?

answers: The LORD’s law leads the nations away from war
The law teaches the nations to prepare for battle
The law causes the nations to separate from one another
challenge.explanation: The law goes forth from Zion, and the nations consequently abandon warfare.
challenge.q: How are instruction and peace connected in this passage?

answers: Israel will walk in the name of the LORD forever
Israel will follow the gods of the nations
Israel will leave the land permanently
challenge.explanation: The peoples walk in the name of their gods, but Israel will walk in the name of the LORD forever.
challenge.q: How are Israel and the other peoples contrasted at the end of the passage?

paragraphs.title: Gathering the Remnant and Restoring the Kingdom

answers: Her that halteth and her that is driven out
The kings of Babylon
The armies of the nations
easy.explanation: The LORD will assemble the one who is lame and gather the one who was driven out.
easy.q: Whom will the LORD assemble in that day?

answers: A remnant
A foreign army
A ruined city
easy.explanation: He will make her that halted a remnant.
easy.q: What will the LORD make her that halted?

answers: In mount Zion
In Babylon
In the wilderness
easy.explanation: The LORD shall reign over them in mount Zion.
easy.q: Where will the LORD reign over them?

answers: They will become a strong nation
They will remain scattered
They will be destroyed
medium.explanation: The LORD will make them a remnant and a strong nation.
medium.q: What will become of the gathered and afflicted people?

answers: A lame or weakened person
A queen leading an army
A builder of the city
medium.explanation: The expression refers to one who is lame or weakened.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “her that halteth” describe?

answers: The first dominion and the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem
The army of Babylon
The law of the nations
medium.explanation: The first dominion and the kingdom will come to the daughter of Jerusalem.
medium.q: What will come unto the tower of the flock?

answers: He can gather the weak and make them a strong nation
He will replace His people with foreign nations
He intends to scatter the remnant further
challenge.explanation: The LORD gathers the afflicted and transforms them into a remnant and strong nation.
challenge.q: What does the LORD’s choice of the lame and scattered suggest?

answers: The gathered people become the community over which the restored kingdom reigns
The gathering prevents any kingdom from returning
The gathering leads directly to another exile
challenge.explanation: The gathered remnant is followed by the coming of the first dominion and kingdom.
challenge.q: How are gathering the remnant and restoring the kingdom related?

answers: It will continue permanently
It will last only briefly
It will occur only during exile
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the lasting and continuing nature of the LORD’s reign.
challenge.q: What does “from henceforth, even for ever” indicate about the LORD’s reign?

paragraphs.title: Exile in Babylon and the Beginning of Redemption

answers: A woman in travail
A king in battle
A farmer at harvest
easy.explanation: Her pains are compared to those of a woman in travail.
easy.q: To what is the daughter of Zion compared?

answers: In the field
In the temple
In Egypt
easy.explanation: The passage says she will go forth out of the city and dwell in the field.
easy.q: Where will the daughter of Zion dwell after going forth from the city?

answers: In Babylon
In mount Zion
At the tower of the flock
easy.explanation: The passage says, “there shalt thou be delivered,” referring to Babylon.

answers: Her king and counsellor are absent, and pangs have taken her
She has received peace and prosperity
The nations have come to learn the law
medium.explanation: The passage asks whether her king and counsellor have perished and says that pangs have taken her.
medium.q: Why does the daughter of Zion cry out aloud?

answers: Endure the pains of childbirth
Leave the city immediately in triumph
Rest because danger has passed
medium.explanation: The command uses the image of a woman suffering labor pains.
medium.q: What does “Be in pain, and labour to bring forth” mean in context?

answers: Pain, departure from the city, exile to Babylon, and deliverance
Deliverance, departure, pain, and return to Babylon
War, peace, rebuilding, and then exile
medium.explanation: The daughter of Zion suffers, leaves the city, goes to Babylon, and is there delivered.
medium.q: What is the order of events in the passage?

answers: Her present suffering is connected with a coming deliverance
It shows that her situation will never change
It means she will immediately conquer her enemies
challenge.explanation: The image joins intense present pain with the expectation of a new future.
challenge.q: Why is the image of childbirth appropriate for the daughter of Zion?

answers: She will leave the city and experience exile
She will immediately build a new city
She will enter the temple in triumph
challenge.explanation: Dwelling in the field follows her departure from the city and precedes her journey to Babylon.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from her dwelling in the field?

answers: It is the place of exile where deliverance will occur
It is the place from which the nations come to learn
It is where the restored kingdom is established
challenge.explanation: She will go to Babylon, but there she will be delivered and redeemed from her enemies.
challenge.q: What role does Babylon play in the sequence?

paragraphs.title: The Nations Gather for Their Defeat

answers: Against Zion
Against Babylon
Against the mountain of the LORD
easy.explanation: Many nations are gathered against Zion.
easy.q: Against whom are many nations gathered?

answers: They want her to be defiled and to look upon her defeat
They want her to teach them the law
They want to join her kingdom
easy.explanation: They say, “Let her be defiled, and let our eye look upon Zion.”
easy.q: What do the nations want to see happen to Zion?

answers: Iron
Gold
Wood
easy.explanation: The LORD will make Zion’s horn iron.
easy.q: What will Zion’s horn be made like?

answers: The thoughts and counsel of the LORD
The road to Jerusalem
The language of Zion
medium.explanation: They do not know the thoughts of the LORD or understand His counsel.
medium.q: What do the nations fail to understand?

answers: Sheaves gathered into the floor
Waters gathered into a river
Trees gathered into a forest
medium.explanation: The LORD will gather them as sheaves into the floor.
medium.q: What are the gathered nations compared to?

answers: Strength to thresh many people
Permission to flee from the city
A new army from Babylon
medium.explanation: The LORD commands the daughter of Zion to arise and thresh, promising strength against many people.
medium.q: What will the LORD give Zion in the final command of the passage?

answers: The nations gather expecting Zion’s defeat, but they are gathered for judgment
Zion expects victory but finally flees
The nations gather to learn, but Zion teaches them warfare
challenge.explanation: The nations do not understand that their gathering serves the LORD’s purpose against them.
challenge.q: What is the central reversal in the passage?

answers: They will be consecrated unto the LORD
They will be given to the kings of the nations
They will be taken to Babylon
challenge.explanation: The LORD says He will consecrate their gain and substance unto the LORD.
challenge.q: What will happen to the gain and substance of the nations?

answers: Zion receives power to overcome the nations gathered against her
Zion loses all power because of the siege
Zion joins the nations in their rebellion
challenge.explanation: After the nations gather against Zion, the LORD gives her strength to thresh many people.
challenge.q: How does the command to arise and thresh complete the passage?
